name: PM-USP CSSS Scholarship
full_name: PM Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan — Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship for College and University Students
summary: A merit scholarship for degree students who finished in the top 20% of their Class 12 board stream.
benefit_note: ₹12,000 a year for the first three years of a degree, and ₹20,000 a year at postgraduate level. Students on five-year integrated or professional courses get ₹20,000 a year in the 4th and 5th year.
how_to_apply: Register on the National Scholarship Portal — the whole application is online.
Enter your Class 12 board result and your college's AISHE code.
Upload your income certificate. Fresh applicants need one; renewals do not.
Your institution verifies the application on the portal.

all.source_quote: Students who are above 80th percentile of successful candidates in the relevant stream from the respective Board of Examination in Class XII of 10+2 pattern or equivalent

curation_notes: DRAFT — not yet read by a human against the official page. Do not ship.

Rules and amounts come from the official CSSS guidelines PDF (CSSS_GUIDLINES_07022024_updated.pdf), downloaded from the National Scholarship Portal and read on 2026-08-09. Dates come from the portal homepage.

THIS SCHEME CONFLICTS WITH PUDHUMAI PENN AND TAMIL PUDHALVAN. CSSS excludes anyone on a 'State run scholarship scheme'; the two Tamil Nadu schemes explicitly allow holding other scholarships. So a Pudhumai Penn recipient appears to be disqualified from CSSS, but not the other way round. This is exactly the scheme-interaction problem behind the decision not to build a benefit stacking optimiser. The card should say the conflict exists and let the user decide — it must not pick for them.

TO CONFIRM: the application window. The portal homepage gives a student application closing date of 31-10-2026, while the All-Scholarships listing shows renewal applications closing 30-09-2026. Those are probably the fresh and renewal windows respectively. The fresh window is used here. Confirm both before this ships, because is_rolling is false and a wrong end date silently hides the scheme.
IGNORE the ₹10,000 figure in section 7 of the guidelines. It is a historical rate for academic year 2021-22, not the current one. The current rate is ₹12,000.

The 80th percentile is of SUCCESSFUL CANDIDATES IN THE RELEVANT STREAM for the student's own board — not a raw mark percentage. The profile question has to be worded carefully or students will answer with their percentage and get a wrong result.
TO CONFIRM: the documents list. The guidelines mention an income certificate for fresh applicants and a bank account in the student's own name; the other two are inferred.
This is the first scheme in the corpus with a real application window and the first with effort_level EASY.
